nodes.summary: Let $L_n$ denote the Lucas numbers. For every integer $m > 1$, every residue modulo $m$ is attained by the Lucas numbers (for every $r$ with $0 \le r < m$ there is $n \ge 0$ with $L_n \equiv r \pmod m$) if and only if $m \in \{2, 4, 6, 7, 14\}$ or $m = 3^k$ for some integer $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Avila–Chen theorem on Lucas numbers modulo $m$

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every integer $m > 1$, with $L_n$ the Lucas numbers, every residue modulo $m$ is attained (for every $r$ with $0 \le r < m$ there is $n \ge 0$ with $L_n \equiv r \pmod m$) if and only if $m \in \{2, 4, 6, 7, 14\}$ or $m = 3^k$ for some integer $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Classification of moduli for which the Lucas numbers attain every residue
